# yantrad

> The Yantra control-plane daemon. Every client talks to this and nothing else; no client ever talks
> directly to a managed machine. An axum server with a read-only JSON API over a background
> snapshot, the writes (`POST /heartbeat`, `new`, and `edit`/`up`/`down`/`resume` per workspace), a
> WebSocket that bridges a workspace's session to a browser, and the dashboard itself. It is an HTTP surface over
> `yantra-core`, not a second copy of the logic.

## Source

- [src/main.rs](src/main.rs): resolves its bind addresses from Tailscale, fails closed, serves `/healthz`, shuts down on SIGTERM. Plain HTTP on 7717; TLS is `tailscale serve`'s (`just https`, port 8443) and never this crate's.
- [src/refresh.rs](src/refresh.rs): one background task per data class, writing `yantra_core::snapshot::Snapshot`. The interval is a constant, low enough to keep the ssh masters warm. No request path touches ssh.
- [src/api.rs](src/api.rs): `GET /api/{machines,workspaces,sessions}`, read-only. Every answer says whether the look succeeded, failed or has not happened, and how old it is. `machines` also carries each machine's latest heartbeat and its age, joined on the node id; `null` there is *never heard from* and is not a beat that reports zero. DTOs live here rather than as `Serialize` on core's types (ADR-0005).
- [src/web.rs](src/web.rs): serves the built dashboard from `YANTRA_WEB`, with a fallback to `index.html` so deep links reach the app. Refuses at startup if that directory holds no `index.html`, and answers a 404 that says how to set it when nothing is configured. Assets are a directory rather than embedded (R-24).
- [src/write.rs](src/write.rs): `POST /api/workspaces`, `PATCH /api/workspaces/{name}` and `POST /api/workspaces/{name}/{up,down,resume}` — the CLI's own verbs and nothing more (`yantra new`, `edit`, `up`, `down`, `resume`). Authorised per ADR-0016: the caller's source address is resolved **live** via `whois`, and a node that is not this owner's, or carries tags, is refused 403. A `tailscale` that cannot answer is **503**, never 403 — nothing was decided about the caller. **Behind `tailscale serve` that check sees the proxy, not the caller** (Y-111, measured; ADR-0016 amendment; Y-118 decides the fix). The verbs that reach a machine await ssh, which the read path may not; `new` touches no machine and answers **409** for a name already taken, returning the created workspace in the body because the read model will not hold it for up to 30 s. `edit` (Y-126) rewrites only the fields the body names — `"startup": null` clears the command, an absent key leaves it, and a body naming nothing is a **400** — and answers the workspace as it now reads, in the same shape `new` answers. It reaches the machine **only** when `machine` really changes, and then refuses rather than strands: a tmux session still open on the machine being left is a **409** (I-30, and `yantra down` clears it), and a machine that could not be asked is a **503** rather than a move (R-23). The refusal is [`edit.rs`](../yantra-core/src/edit.rs)'s; this route only carries it.
- [src/terminal.rs](src/terminal.rs): `GET /api/workspaces/{name}/terminal`, a WebSocket over [`yantra_core::pty`](../yantra-core/src/pty.rs). An upgrade is a `GET`, so it does **not** inherit `write.rs`'s check and calls `allowed()` by name — `up` starts a process Yantra chose, a terminal runs whatever is typed. Frames carry no envelope: binary is terminal bytes both ways, text is control — `{"rows":…,"cols":…,"term":…}` from the browser, required first because a pty opens with a window and a terminal (the `term` is the dashboard's own constant, never a user's — I-36), and a failure reason from the daemon, which a close frame cannot hold. **The stream is never logged** (Q5), and **never buffered**: a browser that lost its socket opens another, and the tmux on the far side draws the pane for whichever client attaches (Y-132). It holds ssh for as long as someone is looking, which the request path may not — and it does so after the upgrade has answered.
- [src/contract.rs](src/contract.rs): tests only. Renders every read route and every write DTO into [`web/src/contract.gen.ts`](../../web/src/contract.gen.ts), TypeScript that `satisfies` the dashboard's own types, and fails when the committed file no longer matches — `just fixtures` rewrites it. The seam between the daemon and the browser, checked rather than kept in step by convention (Y-124).
- [src/heartbeat.rs](src/heartbeat.rs): `POST /heartbeat`, the write `yantra-agent` makes. 204 with an empty body, a 4 KB limit, strict parsing, and identity taken from the source address rather than the payload. Holds `Beats`, one in-memory row per machine keyed on the node id, overwritten every beat.

## What decides its shape

- [ADR-0005](../../docs/adr/0005-core-logic-in-a-library-crate.md): the logic lives in the library; this crate stays thin.
- [ADR-0013](../../docs/adr/0013-the-heartbeat-carries-only-what-placement-scores.md): what `POST /heartbeat` accepts, why it answers nothing, and why the source address is the identity.
- [ADR-0004](../../docs/adr/0004-rust-for-the-daemon.md): Rust, with axum and tokio. TypeScript belongs to the browser — do not introduce a second runtime here.
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): what is already settled, and what to read before starting — including why there is no `--bind` flag.

## Optional

- [tracker.md](tracker.md): the invariants waiting here for the daemon that does not exist yet — SQLite, scheduling, PTY. None of them exercised by shipped code.
- [../../tracker.md](../../tracker.md): M4 is the milestone that needs this. Open decisions that affect it are listed there.
- [docs/vision.md](../../docs/vision.md): what the daemon is ultimately for.
